problem: Serve high traffic efficiently with a small engineering team.
title: Stack Overflow scales up a monolith on a small number of powerful servers
context: Stack Overflow served very large traffic with a mostly monolithic application and few servers.
decision_made: Prefer a scale-up strategy, buying bigger machines with more memory when limits are hit, and keep nearly all work in a web tier and database.
action_taken: Documented the architecture publicly in posts and talks from 2013 to 2016.
observed_outcome: A High Scalability update described about 560 million page views a month on about 25 servers with web servers at low CPU load; a 2015 talk cited about 4 billion requests a month.
lessons: A well-tuned monolith on strong hardware can serve very large traffic, and distributing is not always needed.
limitations: Figures differ across sources and years. The 2016 post's own server and page-view counts were not retrieved. Stack Overflow's scale and read-heavy workload may not match other products.

claims.claim_text: Stack Overflow used a scale-up strategy, buying bigger machines when it hit limits.
High Scalability reported about 560 million page views a month on about 25 servers.
